title: Oligonucleotide Therapeutics Market Outlook 2026-2035 - Featuring Profiles of Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Ionis Pharmaceuticals, and Sarepta Therapeutics
author: Researchandmarkets.Com
description: The global oligonucleotide therapeutics market is projected to grow from USD 7.7 billion in 2025 to USD 72.1 billion by 2035, expanding at a 23.4% CAGR. Growth is driven by advances in RNA-based medicine, targeted delivery technologies, expanding applications beyond rare diseases into chronic and metabolic conditions, and increasing regulatory approvals. Antisense oligonucleotides lead the market at 39.9% share, while subcutaneous administration dominates at 56.4%. North America commands 57.9% market share.

title: Set Yourself Up for a Strong 2027: 2 Pharmaceutical Stocks to Buy in September
author: James Brumley

title: Pfizer Stock Rises Almost 9% in 3 Months: Time to Buy, Hold or Exit?
author: Na
description: Pfizer's stock has risen 8.6% in three months as investors gain confidence in the company's ability to offset declining COVID-19 product sales with growth from non-COVID products, which grew 18% operationally in Q2. The company is pursuing ambitious pipelines in oncology and obesity, with plans for 10 Phase III studies for berobenatide targeting first approvals in 2028. However, Pfizer faces headwinds from a $1.1B revenue impact from patent expirations and expects 2026 revenue to decline slightly to $60.5-$62.5 billion. Despite these challenges, the stock trades at an attractive valuation with a 6.2% dividend yield, and analysts maintain a Hold rating with expectations for high single-digit revenue growth from 2029 onward.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Pfizer shows mixed signals: positive momentum from non-COVID product growth (18% operational growth in Q2), strong pipeline development, and attractive valuation with 6.2% dividend yield support a positive outlook. However, this is offset by declining COVID revenues, upcoming patent cliff ($1.1B impact in 2026), flat 2026 guidance, and lagging position in the obesity market behind competitors. The Hold rating reflects this balance.

BioNTech's partnership with Pfizer on Comirnaty is experiencing significant revenue decline as COVID-19 normalization continues, with sales expected to drop to approximately $4 billion in 2026 from $6.7 billion in 2025.
Eli Lilly is mentioned as a leader in the obesity market, ahead of Pfizer in this high-growth therapeutic area, indicating competitive strength and market position.
Novo Nordisk is identified as a leader in the obesity market alongside Eli Lilly, demonstrating strong competitive positioning in this growing therapeutic segment.

title: Is Novo Nordisk Stock Still Too Cheap for Investors to Ignore?
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: Novo Nordisk's stock has declined 66% from its 2024 high and now trades at attractive valuations compared to historical averages. While the company lost its GLP-1 weight-loss drug market lead to Eli Lilly, it is attempting a comeback through a new GLP-1 pill and a volume-driven pricing strategy. Despite significant uncertainty around its competitive position and business transition, the stock's low valuation and 3.7% dividend yield may appeal to value and dividend investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock is attractively valued with low P/E and P/S ratios plus a solid dividend yield, but faces significant uncertainty regarding its ability to regain market share from Eli Lilly and the success of its volume-driven business model transition. The company has both positive valuation metrics and competitive headwinds.

Eli Lilly has established itself as the industry leader in the GLP-1 weight-loss drug market, successfully taking market share from first-mover Novo Nordisk and recently introducing its own GLP-1 pill, demonstrating strong competitive positioning.

title: Novo Nordisk's Semaglutide Meets Goal in Pediatric Obesity Study
author: Na
description: Novo Nordisk announced positive phase III STEP Young study results showing semaglutide reduced BMI in children aged 6-12 with obesity, with 40.4% no longer classified as obese after 68 weeks. However, the company faces mounting competitive pressure from Eli Lilly's superior weight-loss drugs and emerging biotech competitors in the GLP-1 obesity treatment market.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Positive clinical trial results for semaglutide in children support pipeline strength, but stock performance lags industry (+16.4% vs -5.3% YTD) and intensifying competition from Eli Lilly and smaller biotechs limits upside potential.

Mounjaro and Zepbound demonstrate superior weight-loss efficacy compared to Novo Nordisk's semaglutide, gaining market share steadily. Recent FDA approval of oral GLP-1 drug Foundayo strengthens competitive position in obesity market.
